title: He didn’t just hate a man.
paragraphs: He didn’t just hate a man.
He wanted an entire people erased.

What kind of heart wakes up one day and says,
“Because I was dishonored… they all must die”?

What kind of pride grows so deep
it turns a personal offense into a national genocide?
Promoted. Trusted. Elevated in the palace.

Wounded ego.
Uncontrolled pride.
Unchecked bitterness.
And when Mordecai refused to bow, something snapped.
“But when Haman saw that Mordecai did not bow down or pay him homage, Haman was filled with fury.” — Esther 3:5
That’s what happens when pride is not surrendered—it doesn’t stay small.
You may not be planning genocide.
But have you ever replayed an offense in your head… over and over?
Have you ever felt that quiet satisfaction imagining someone getting what they “deserve”?
Have you ever let one wound define how you see people?

Manipulated the king.
Distorted truth.
Weaponized influence.
“There is a certain people scattered abroad… their laws are different… it is not to the king’s profit to tolerate them.” — Esther 3:8
It will preach lies that feel like logic.
It will make destruction feel like justice.
You can stand in a place of authority…
And still be completely ruled by sin.

Before Haman plotted,
God positioned Esther.

Before the decree was signed,
God preserved a remnant.

Before the trap was sprung,
God had already written the ending.
The moment pride collapses under its own weight.
Became the place of his own destruction.
“So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai.” — Esther 7:10
He died on what he designed.
Scripture confirms it again and again:
“Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.” — Proverbs 16:18

Some scholars interpret this not just as poetic wisdom,
but as a spiritual law woven into reality itself.
But don’t miss the deeper layer.
Because Haman is not just a villain.
Every time you refuse to forgive…
Every time you elevate yourself above others…
You are walking the same road.
“Though He was in the form of God… He emptied Himself… becoming obedient to the point of death—even death on a cross.” — Philippians 2:6–8
Haman built gallows for the innocent.
Jesus carried a cross for the guilty.
You and I are not just victims of sin.
Christ took the punishment that pride deserves.
“God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.” — James 4:6
That means if we cling to pride…
And here’s the hope that will wreck you in the best way:
You don’t have to die on the gallows you built.
Jesus already took your place on the cross.
So now the question is not about Haman.
What bitterness have you baptized as “righteous”?
Because the same God who brought down Haman…
Is the same God ready to lift you up.
Today can be your turning point.

From pride to surrender.
From hatred to healing.
From hidden sin to open grace.
If your heart is ready, pray this:

“Jesus, break my pride.
Search me. Clean me. Change me.
I surrender every hidden bitterness.
Give me Your heart.
I trust in Your cross alone. Amen.”
If this hit you deep, don’t ignore it.
Come back to it. Let it confront you again.
If this stirred something in you…
